title: First flight
source: Charter first-flight.md: power on, connect through a gateway, Takeoff, Move To, Land, with the failure branch.

branches.failsafe: If the link drops during Move To (replaces the main steps after Move To starts)

steps.why: The drone opens the link through the gateway and says which protocol version it speaks.
Core accepts the drone and confirms the version both sides will use.
The drone reports its current settings, so Core knows what it will do if the link drops.
The drone reports it is healthy and ready.
The drone reports where it is on the ground.
The drone reports its battery, on its own schedule.
Core queues Task T1: climb straight up to 30 m above home.
Core queues Task T2 straight away: fly to a position, keeping the current altitude.
Core queues Task T3: go to 20 m, fly back over the landing spot and land.
Tasks were added, so the drone reports its queue. Core sees all 3 arrived; a missing one would be resent.
The drone reports it started T1 (Takeoff).
The drone reports its climb.
The drone reports T1 done: it is holding at 30 m.
The drone reports it started T2 (Move To), the next Task in its queue.
The drone reports its position and speed on the way.
The drone reports its battery.
The drone reports T2 done: it is over the destination.
The drone reports it started T3 (Land), the last Task in its queue.
The drone reports it is back on the ground.
The drone reports T3 done. Its queue is now empty, so the run is over.
The drone reports its battery after landing.
Partway through Move To, the drone loses the gateway (the trigger) and returns to home (its link_loss_response setting). It sends this as soon as it can be heard again.
The drone reports T2 failed, so Core's record matches what happened.
The drone cancels the rest of its queue, so T3 (Land) is reported cancelled.
The drone reports its position on the way home.
The last Task finishing (an empty queue) marks the end of the run, but nothing covers the Reset ZIP yet. Not needed on the wire yet; listed so it is not forgotten.
